cards.name: Bitget Card
cards.tagline: Spend crypto in 180+ countries with up to 8% cashback.
cards.description: Bitget's card is built for exchange power users: stake BGB or hit VIP tiers to unlock the headline 8% cashback, and use USDT on Tron to keep top-up costs low. The fee stack is middle-of-the-road, but country coverage is excellent.

cards.name: BitPay Card
cards.tagline: Convert crypto to fiat and spend anywhere Mastercard is accepted.
cards.description: BitPay's card is a legacy prepaid product with a high fee stack: 1.5% to load and 3% on foreign spend. It remains useful for US users who want a physical Mastercard tied to BitPay's merchant network, but it is no longer competitive on cost.

cards.name: Bleap
cards.tagline: A self-custody Visa built for stablecoin natives.
cards.description: Bleap is a newer entrant focused on stablecoin holders who want self-custody without the clunky UX of early DeFi cards. FX at 0.4% is among the lowest in the category, and the 0.5% conversion fee is fair. The main risk is that the product is young.

cards.name: Bybit Card
cards.tagline: Spend USDT and BTC with up to 10% cashback paid in BTC.
cards.topup_fee_notes: 1% crypto top-up; free USDT on Arbitrum
cards.staking_requirement: None; VIP tiers unlock higher caps
cards.description: Bybit's card leans on promotional cashback: the headline 10% is capped and category-specific, while the base rate is closer to 2%. It is still one of the most generous exchange cards, and full Apple Pay support makes it easy to deploy stablecoins for daily spend.
pros: No annual fee and instant virtual issuance
Works with Apple Pay and Google Pay

cards.name: Coinbase Card
cards.tagline: Earn up to 4% back in BTC or ETH on everyday spending.
cards.atm_fee_text: Free at Allpoint ATMs in the US
cards.description: Coinbase Card is the lowest-friction way for US and EEA users to spend a Coinbase balance. Rewards rotate by promotion and asset, so the 4% headline is not guaranteed, but the 0% FX policy and deep exchange liquidity make it a dependable travel card.
pros: Rewards paid in your choice of crypto
Backed by a publicly listed exchange
cons: Reward rate varies by promotion and region
Full KYC and exchange account required

cards.name: CoinJar Card
cards.tagline: Australia's crypto debit card with 1% back in BTC.
cards.description: CoinJar's card is a straightforward Australian debit card with bitcoin cashback and no annual fee. It is inexpensive for domestic spend, but the 2.5% FX fee and 1% crypto conversion fee make it a poor choice for travel.

cards.name: Crypto.com Visa
cards.tagline: The original crypto cashback card, from Ruby Steel to Obsidian.
cards.atm_fee_text: Free up to tier allowance, then 2%
cards.requirements_text: Full KYC; CRO stake for higher tiers
cards.description: Crypto.com's Visa line is the most established in the category. The five-tier ladder is still the clearest way to buy lounge access and streaming rebates with a card stake, though the headline cashback now depends on CRO price and lock-up terms. A safe default for mainstream spenders.
pros: Mature app, card and support ecosystem
Lounge access and streaming rebates at mid tiers
Physical metal cards from Jade Green upward
cons: Cashback is paid in CRO and requires a stake
Tier economics shift with CRO price

cards.name: Deblock
cards.tagline: A crypto-native current account with a Visa card and 0% FX.
perks: Crypto and fiat in one app
cards.description: Deblock positions itself as a crypto-native neobank rather than a card product: a real IBAN, SEPA transfers, a Visa card and self-custody wallet access in one app. Fee transparency is excellent, though the 1% crypto conversion fee adds up for frequent top-ups.

cards.name: DolarApp
cards.tagline: Dollar account and card for Latin America, funded with USDC.
cards.description: DolarApp is built for Latin Americans who earn in stablecoins and spend in dollars. The card is simple and cheap for USD purchases, with USDC on Base keeping funding costs at zero. Coverage is limited to the region, but within it the product is hard to beat.

cards.name: ether.fi Cash
cards.tagline: Self-custody Visa with 3% cashback on everything, paid in ETH.
cards.fx_fee_notes: 0% FX on all currencies; no weekend markup
cards.topup_fee_notes: No top-up or liquidation fee on supported assets
cards.description: ether.fi Cash turns your on-chain balance into a spendable Visa without giving up custody. Balances stay in your wallet until the moment of purchase, cashback lands in ETH, and FX is genuinely free — no 0.5% weekend surcharge. It is the benchmark for DeFi-native spending in 2026.
pros: Real self-custody: funds stay in your wallet until settlement
3%+ cashback paid in ETH, with no annual fee
0% FX and no crypto-to-fiat top-up spread
Full Apple Pay and Google Pay support
cons: Light KYC required, so not a true no-KYC option
ATM withdrawals cost 2.5% after the monthly allowance
Cashback boost requires locking $10,000 in the Luxe tier

cards.name: Fold Card
cards.tagline: Bitcoin rewards on debit spending, plus a spin-to-earn game.
cards.description: Fold is a Bitcoin-first debit card with a gamified rewards layer. The base cashback is modest, but the occasional boosted merchants and spin wheel can push effective returns higher. Best for US Bitcoin maximalists who already use the Fold app.

cards.name: Gemini Credit Card
cards.tagline: A real credit card that rewards you in crypto, instantly.
cards.requirements_text: Full KYC, US residency, credit check
cards.description: Gemini's card is a genuine credit card issued by WebBank, with rewards deposited into your Gemini account instantly. The 4% rate is category-capped (dining), but the 1% base, zero FX fee and no annual fee make it a strong everyday card for US crypto holders.
pros: True credit card with no annual fee
cons: Category caps on top reward rate

cards.name: Gnosis Pay
cards.tagline: Spend EURe and GNO straight from your Safe. Zero FX, on-chain settlement.
cards.fx_fee_notes: 0% FX for EEA/UK card spend; interbank rate
cards.atm_fee_text: Free at any ATM in the EEA (fair-use limits)
cards.topup_fee_notes: Top up with EURe or USDC at 0%
cards.requirements_text: Full KYC, EEA/UK residency, Safe wallet
cards.description: Gnosis Pay is the most 'bank-like' self-custody card in Europe: a Safe smart account, a real IBAN, SEPA transfers and a Visa that settles on-chain. Spending EURe avoids conversion entirely, and the 0% FX policy makes it a strong travel companion.
pros: True self-custody through a Safe smart account
0% FX and free EEA ATM withdrawals
Real IBAN and SEPA rails alongside the card
Up to 2% back in GNO when staking
cons: Full KYC and EEA/UK residency required

cards.name: Holyheld
cards.tagline: Cash out crypto to any Visa card with a 0.9% flat fee.
cards.description: Holyheld is less a card and more a cash-out rail: you top up a virtual Visa from self-custody with a flat 0.9% fee. It is transparent and useful for occasional spend, but there is no physical card, no rewards to speak of, and the fee applies on both ends.
cons: Double 0.9% fee on top-up and FX

cards.name: Kast
cards.tagline: Stablecoin card with up to 10% yield and premium metal options.
cards.requirements_text: No KYC for starter tier; full KYC for yield
cards.description: Kast combines a stablecoin card with a yield account, which is either a killer feature or a regulatory question mark depending on your appetite. The starter tier is genuinely low-friction, the metal card feels premium, and USDC on Base keeps top-up costs near zero.
pros: High stablecoin yield on parked balances

cards.name: Kraken Card
cards.tagline: Kraken's debit card with 0% FX and instant USDC spending.
cards.fx_fee_notes: 0% FX at the Visa network rate
cards.description: Kraken's card is deliberately boring in the best way: hold USDC, spend USDC, pay no FX. There is no points game or stake requirement, which makes it a strong choice for people who want exchange-grade custody and a clean fee schedule rather than a rewards programme.

cards.name: Ledger Live Card
cards.tagline: Hardware-wallet-native card for EEA and UK.
cards.requirements_text: Full KYC, EEA/UK residency, Ledger device
cards.description: Ledger's card is aimed at people who already keep assets on a Ledger and want to spend without moving them to an exchange. The hardware-backed approval flow is reassuring, and 0% FX is competitive. The trade-off is a heavier onboarding process and EEA/UK-only availability.

cards.name: MetaMask Card
cards.tagline: Spend from your self-custody wallet via Mastercard.
cards.description: MetaMask's card is the most anticipated self-custody product of 2026. It draws directly from the wallet, avoids FX fees during the pilot, and works anywhere Mastercard is accepted. Availability is still limited to US users, and the rollout has been waitlist-gated.

cards.name: Nexo Card
cards.tagline: Borrow against crypto and spend up to $50k without selling a satoshi.
cards.topup_fee_notes: No top-up fee — credit line against collateral
cards.staking_requirement: Collateralized credit line; NEXO stake for boosts
cards.description: Nexo's card is a credit card in the literal sense: you borrow against your crypto collateral and repay in fiat or stablecoins. That makes it the cleanest way to spend during a bull market without triggering a taxable disposal, provided you are comfortable with leverage.
pros: No need to sell crypto to spend
Credit line up to $50,000 depending on collateral
cons: Leverage risk if collateral prices fall
FX fee unless you reach Platinum

cards.name: OKX Card
cards.tagline: Self-custody OKX Wallet card for EEA spenders.
cards.requirements_text: Light KYC, EEA residency, OKX Wallet
cards.description: OKX's card is a virtual-only Mastercard that draws from the self-custody OKX Wallet. It is a useful companion for DeFi users in Europe who want Apple Pay without moving funds to a centralized exchange, though the lack of a physical card limits it.

cards.name: Plutus Card
cards.tagline: Stake PLU for up to 8% cashback and airport lounge access.
cards.requirements_text: Full KYC, UK/EEA residency, PLU stake
cards.description: Plutus still offers one of the highest nominal cashback rates in Europe, but the 8% ceiling requires a large PLU stake, a monthly reward cap and a subscription. The card works well for high-spend users who are comfortable with token risk; casual users will find the fee stack and reward mechanics frustrating.

cards.name: RedotPay
cards.tagline: A virtual Visa for ad spend and travel with light KYC and global reach.
cards.topup_fee_notes: 1.2% crypto top-up; 0% for USDT on Tron
cards.requirements_text: No KYC for tier 1; ID required above $1,000
cards.description: RedotPay is the go-to option for people who need a working virtual card today. The $10 virtual card is issued in minutes with minimal onboarding, works on most ad platforms, and supports USDT on Tron at zero top-up fee. Fees are higher than DeFi-native rivals, but availability is unmatched.
pros: Widely accepted for Facebook and Google Ads
Supports USDT on Tron with 0% top-up
cons: Custodial — you do not hold the keys
ID required once you exceed the no-KYC limit

cards.name: Shakepay Card
cards.tagline: Canada's no-fee Visa with bitcoin cashback and weekly shakes.
cards.description: Shakepay's card is one of the few genuinely competitive Canadian crypto cards, with up to 2% back in bitcoin and no annual fee. The 2.5% FX fee makes it a poor travel companion, so keep it for domestic spend.

cards.name: Wirex Card
cards.tagline: Multi-currency crypto account with WXT rewards and 40+ currencies.
cards.fx_fee_notes: 0% FX in 40+ currencies; weekend spread may apply
perks: Crypto and fiat in one account
cards.staking_requirement: WXT stake for Premium and Elite
cards.description: Wirex pioneered the crypto debit card and still has one of the widest fiat currency selections. It is a solid everyday card for expats who hold multiple currencies, but the reward rate has been diluted over the years and the fee schedule is busier than newer DeFi rivals.
pros: Supports both crypto and fiat balances
Established brand with a long track record
